name: McCORMACK, the Hon. Michael Francis

headline.note: Private newspaper work is established from 1981 to 2002, followed by publishing in 2002–2010. Explicit full-time evidence now supports the initial cadetship, whose end is unknown; it is not extended to later roles. MSS legal entity and newspaper family control are documented. Unresolved boundaries, leave, later hours and overlaps prevent public/private full-time totals.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies record acting-editor service in 1991–1992. Exact dates, hours and leave are unresolved. CSU archives support private family control during this employment; the 2007 Rural Press acquisition was later. The member’s current general biography dates editorship to1991, whereas the detailed official chronology distinguishes acting1991–1992 from editor1992 onward. This may reflect compressed wording; preserve the detailed phases pending appointment records rather than silently changing the start.
career_spells.counting_note: This title transition is retained separately without inventing calendar boundaries.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official records give 1992–2002; a Wagga Wagga historical-society publication supplies an exact 1 March 1992 editor appointment. Charles Sturt University archives corroborate the editor years, and contemporaneous ABC reporting places suspension and departure in February 2002. The historical publication says the successor followed on 15 July 2002; that later succession date is retained as a vacancy/transition conflict, not substituted for McCormack's departure. Exact cessation day, hours and leave remain unresolved. CSU archives support private family control during this employment; the 2007 Rural Press acquisition was later. A September 2003 ABC report confirms an out-of-court dismissal settlement, not continued work through that date. The member’s current general biography dates editorship to1991, whereas the detailed official chronology distinguishes acting1991–1992 from editor1992 onward. Preserve the detailed phases and explicit conflicts.
career_spells.counting_note: The private-media employer and broad continuity are established, but mixed-precision boundaries and missing full-time evidence prevent an exact duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies and McCormack's published history record the group-editor appointment from 1996 within the continuing Daily Advertiser editorship. Exact scope, transition date, hours and leave are unresolved. CSU archives support private family control during this employment; the 2007 Rural Press acquisition was later.
career_spells.counting_note: This concurrent senior title must not be added to the underlying newspaper employment.

career_spells.employer: McCormack Sheather Shaw Pty Ltd (later MSS Media Pty Ltd), trading as MSS Media Services and Solutions
career_spells.evidence_note: Official publisher range remains 2002–2010. ABR identifies the legal company and registered trading name, resolving the entity gap. The exact election-day endpoint is removed: it was not an employment cessation date. Later company registration/renaming does not establish continued personal work. Clients, hours, leave, ownership changes and actual cessation remain unknown. First-person Sydney Institute address published 28 July 2017 (text dated 26 July) explicitly describes operating a publishing business, purchasing work from a Wagga Wagga printing firm and deriving family income from small business for approximately eight years. This establishes personal commercial activity and income, beyond mere ownership, but neither names the printing client/supplier nor fixes dates or full-time hours. The retrospective eight-year description is not converted into a countable full-time duration.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may count only when substantive full-time work and boundaries are supported; ownership and title alone are insufficient.

career_spells.evidence_note: McCormack's published history and secondary synthesis record the 1994–2003 directorship. Remuneration, workload, exact dates and the historian arrangement are unresolved; the role overlapped newspaper employment and MSS.
career_spells.counting_note: Sporting-club governance is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.employer: Rotary International — District9700 / unidentified Wagga Wagga Rotary club
career_spells.role: Group Study Exchange participant; Rotary club member
career_spells.evidence_note: Party-controlled biography identifies Group Study Exchange participation in1993 and Rotary club membership in his hometown.1993 is an exchange-year observation only, not a year-long course or membership term. Host, destination, exact trip dates, funding, newspaper leave and membership boundaries remain unknown. His4December2018 first-person House speech identifies District9700 and exchange destinations Maine, New Hampshire and Massachusetts, with a Kennebunkport visit. This resolves district and destination, not exact trip dates, host club, funding or newspaper leave. Nearby speakers and the US president’s public career are not McCormack employment evidence.
career_spells.counting_note: Study exchange/community association excluded; no new paid job or full-time employment interval inferred.

research_notes: The official newspaper chronology is preserved as sequential title spells; the group-editor role overlaps the Daily Advertiser editorship and is not double-counted.
The Daily Advertiser and Riverina Media Group are treated as private media employers at the time.
MSS is treated as private self-employment, but founding and publishing titles do not establish full-time work or exact continuity through the 2010 campaign.
Turf Club governance, party campaign roles, party office and federal elected office are separated and excluded under the codebook.
No private full-time total is calculated because exact boundaries, hours, leave and the substantive status of MSS remain unsupported.

2026-10-01 follow-up separates explicitly full-time cadetship from the broader official reporter interval, adds the earlier ground-announcer role and four sporting organisation roles, and identifies MSS company/ABN history. Election day is removed as an unsupported business cessation date.

Searched public professional posts, registry history, employer ownership archives, member career and first-speech material, exact newspaper entry/exit dates, business clients and dismissal reporting. Full-time evidence applies only to the initial cadetship. ABC’s original suspension page was inaccessible but its September 2003 settlement report was retrieved. An anniversary post with relative timestamp does not justify an exact start date. Unrelated namesakes and other workers’ full-time arrangements excluded.

Second follow-up2October2026: employer/cadetship, exact commencement, dismissal newsletters, company sale and client searches did not resolve cadetship completion, later full-time status or MSS cessation. The member’s general1991 editor wording is documented against the detailed acting/editor chronology; no new countable interval. UQ newspaper-history newsletters16/17 returned403 and were not retried. Public indexed snippets insufficient to identify exact suspension/dismissal dates. A15November1981 date in the member’s2020 sports interview dates league reorganisation, not his employment commencement. Relative forty-year anniversary remains insufficient for an exact start. No substantive new employment fact established; do not count this as materially enriched.

Third follow-up3October2026: first-person road-safety article places McCormack on a Daily Advertiser cadet-reporter shift in February1984, proving the cadet phase continued at least into that month. It does not resolve the cadetship end, later reporter/editor full-time status, leave or MSS boundaries, so the headline total remains null.

Fourth follow-up4October2026: Wagga Wagga historical-society publication supplies exact editor appointment1March1992 and successor commencement15July2002. The appointment refines the editor start. The successor date is retained as a vacancy/transition conflict with contemporaneous February2002 departure evidence, not used to extend employment. Hours, leave, cadet end and MSS cessation remain unresolved.

Follow-up2026-10-04: New original 2017 Sydney Institute speech resolves actual commercial operation/income evidence for MSS: own publishing business purchased printing services and supported the family for approximately eight years. No full-time hours or boundaries supplied; headline remains null. Cadet completion and MSS clients/cessation searches did not resolve remaining gaps. Existing biography co-authorship listings do not establish separate paid employment. Defer exhausted generic searches until a dated contract, appointment or employment record supplies a new lead.

Follow-up2026-10-05: Newly checked Nationals personal biography records previously omitted1999 NSW JP appointment and1993 Rotary Group Study Exchange, added separately as excluded community service/study with term and leave gaps. Responsible NSW department confirms volunteer witness/certification nature; current description is not retroactive individual payroll evidence or continuous-term proof. Targeted company tender/client and cadetship-completion searches returned prior ABR and career chronology and unrelated US MSS Media agency. Gold And Glory trademark listing is only a product/registry lead, not a new personal job. Cadet end, later-role hours/leave and MSS exact cessation still unresolved; future original appointment, publishing contract or exchange leave evidence needed. No totals calculated.

Second targeted primary pass2026-10-05: New first-person4December2018 House speech resolves1993 Rotary exchange district9700 and destinations Maine/New Hampshire/Massachusetts, retained within held study/community spell. Specific Kennebunkport episode may lead to contemporary club exchange records; no exact leave/absence dates inferred from external historic missile strike or a planned presidential meeting. Original APH Hansard index https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Hansard/Hansard_Display?bid=chamber%2Fhansardr%2F94aec17b-432c-4e5b-80ed-7c316c83ad31%2F&sid=0191 corroborates exchange text, original reader Internal Error; readable Hansard reproduction clearly separates McCormack5:03pm speech from adjacent Gosling/Kelly. Club searches otherwise returned US namesake and later peace-day appearances; honorary membership remark in another MP speech not attributed to McCormack. Future useful avenue: District9700 original1993 outbound-team itinerary or newspaper leave record; no FT duration calculated.

Third targeted pass2026-10-06: Re-ran exact Riverina Media Group dismissal/judgment, McCormack Sheather Shaw and MSS Media Services and Solutions searches. Results repeated the held February2002 suspension, September2003 out-of-court settlement, self-reported2002–2010 MSS range and public profile; no industrial judgment, cessation day, client contract, ownership change, hours or campaign leave emerged. The inaccessible University of Queensland newspaper-history item was searched by exact title and domain with no result. Social-media summaries and derivative biography claims were not adopted. These routes are exhausted pending an original settlement/employer record, contract or company filing tied to personal work.
